items.title: Amendment 5: a third way to open one, after a capture instance switch
items.text: to_delta(snapshot="chunked", snapshot_on_switch=True) opens a chunked snapshot in the running generation after the batch that first reads a newer capture instance, at that instance's start LSN, which the stream has read past (ADR 0023 Amendment 7). For this ADR it is one more open: the newest, so it supersedes one still open; read by backfill() and applied by silver like the others; completed by a 'bootstrap' row; holding the mode. What differs is its Delta keys: by S (<app_id>#snapopen.<S>, <app_id>#snapdone.<S>), since the generation's keys may be taken by the generation's own snapshot, and its open's switch_batch_id tells backfill() which key its completion takes. Its S is no max_lsn after the batch, so Amendment 2's position (a chunked snapshot's S, which the stream has read up to) still holds; the whole snapshot of snapshot="full" stays above it, as before.

items.title: Amendment 6: chunks cut on a column that is not unique
items.text:
A capture instance of a table without a primary key or unique index has no index_column_list, so snapshot_plan found no key and the snapshot was one chunk: the whole table in one read and one wave, what the chunked mode exists to avoid. Such tables are often the large ones (logs, staging heaps).

  • The snapshotKeys option names the columns. It already cut the snapshot reader's ranges on other columns for reconcile; to_delta(..., snapshot="chunked") now opens the snapshot on them too, unique or not, and records them as the open's keys in the plans table, the columns its chunks are cut on, as before. The plan, the waves (the reader gets them as its snapshotKeys) and each last_bound search take the open's keys, so a plan never moves to other columns; a backfill() whose stream would cut on others (the option changed or dropped, or the unique index changed, the check it replaces) raises. A full snapshot reads the option as it did, for its numPartitions ranges. The one snapshot_on_switch opens (Amendment 5) takes the option as any other open does.
  • Checked at the open. A column CDC does not capture, of a type no bound can be bound as (key_types gives None: time, a 100 ns type ahead of the last column) or one SQL Server cannot sort (bit, which has no MIN or MAX, text, ntext, image, xml) raises ValueError before anything is recorded, instead of a one-chunk plan. The unique index's own columns are not checked, as before.
  • Ranges of values, never a value split. Bounds are values and each chunk the range [lo, hi) of _key_select, so a row is in exactly one chunk whatever repeats, and every row of a value in the same one; NULL sorts first, into the first chunk (an integer column's plan counts no NULL, so they all join it). One integer column is planned from per-slice counts as an integer key is: a slice of one value is never counted again, so a value held by more than chunk_rows rows is a chunk of its own. Other columns walk key_bound seeks, and there the (n + 1)-th row from lo can hold lo's value, which would end the chunk where it starts and the walk would never move: equal in Python, or equal only on SQL Server (a case-insensitive collation's 'n' and 'N', trailing spaces). When the columns are not the unique index's, each bound is therefore checked by one more key_bound seek, of the first row in [lo, bound); when there is none, the seek is repeated twice as far until there is. The chunk then starts on a value held by more than chunk_rows rows and holds fewer than twice its rows. last_bound checks the first key after MAX the same way, past MAX's own copies. Plans on the unique index make the same reads as before.
  • Bronze only. Without a key, silver cannot MERGE: apply_changes refuses a capture instance without a unique index unless given keys that identify a row, as before, and its range deletes still need silver's key to be the open's keys. A row whose cut column changes while the snapshot is read can be read by two chunks or by none; its change rows after S are in bronze, but nothing ties them to a row, so the documentation asks for a column the writers do not update.
  • Cost: on a column no index leads, each seek and each chunk read scans the table, which a unique index never made the plan do. Documented rather than replaced by one NTILE pass: the chunk reads scan anyway, and an index is the fix for both.
  • State: no new key; keys keeps its meaning, the columns the chunks are cut on. A release before 0.8.0 resuming such a snapshot finds keys unlike its unique index and raises in backfill(); its apply_changes applies the waves by key alone unless its keys are the open's.
  • Considered: a backfill(chunk_key=...) argument. The extent (MIN, MAX) is read at the open, right after S, so the columns must be known there; and a fan-out (ADR 0027) gives each table its own options, where one argument would cut every table on one column.
  • Considered: a new client method that seeks the first key above lo. Exact, one seek, but a new member of the CdcClient protocol (ADR 0030) that a client of a user's own would lack; the doubling uses the seeks clients already make.
